rows.stem: The diameter of a wheel is 63 cm. The distance travelled by the wheel in 100 revolutions is :
rows.solution:
The wheel has diameter 63 cm, so its circumference is \(\pi d = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 63 = 198\) cm. In one revolution it travels one circumference.

In 100 revolutions it travels \(100 \times 198 = 19800\) cm \(= 198\) m, which is option (B) 198 m.

rows.stem: The mean of seven observations is 17. If the mean of the first four observations is 15 and that of the last four observations is 18, then the fourth observation is :
rows.solution:
The sum of all seven observations is \(7 \times 17 = 119\).

The first four add to \(4 \times 15 = 60\) and the last four to \(4 \times 18 = 72\). Together these count the fourth observation twice, so \(60 + 72 = 119 + x_4\).

\(x_4 = 132 - 119 = 13\), which is option (B) \(13\).

rows.stem: The distance of the point \((4, 0)\) from x-axis is :
rows.solution:
The distance of a point from the x-axis is the absolute value of its y-coordinate. For \((4, 0)\) that is 0: the point lies on the x-axis.

This is option (C) 0 units.

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are zeroes of the polynomial \(p(x) = kx^2 - 30x + 45k\) and \(\alpha + \beta = \alpha\beta\), then the value of ‘k’ is :
rows.solution:
For \(kx^2 - 30x + 45k\): \(\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{30}{k}\) and \(\alpha\beta = \dfrac{45k}{k} = 45\).

\(\dfrac{30}{k} = 45\), so \(k = \dfrac{30}{45} = \dfrac{2}{3}\), which is option (D) \(\dfrac{2}{3}\).

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: The radii ‘r’ of a sphere and that of the base of a cone are same. If their volumes are also same, then the height of the cone is :
rows.solution:
\(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\). Dividing both sides by \(\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2\): \(h = 4r\).

This is option (D) \(4r\).

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: If in a lottery, there are 10 prizes and 30 blanks, then the probability of winning a prize is :
rows.solution:
There are \(10 + 30 = 40\) tickets, of which 10 win a prize.

\(P(\text{winning a prize}) = \dfrac{10}{40} = \dfrac{1}{4}\), which is option (A) \(\dfrac{1}{4}\).

rows.stem: If \(\tan A + \cot A = 6\), then find the value of \(\tan^2 A + \cot^2 A - 4\).
rows.solution:
Square the given relation: \((\tan A + \cot A)^2 = 36\), that is \(\tan^2 A + \cot^2 A + 2\tan A\cot A = 36\).

Since \(\tan A\cot A = 1\), \(\tan^2 A + \cot^2 A = 36 - 2 = 34\).

So \(\tan^2 A + \cot^2 A - 4 = 34 - 4 = 30\).

rows.subtopic: Probability with Cards, Dice and Coins
rows.stem:
All face cards of spades are removed from a pack of 52 playing cards and the remaining pack is shuffled well. A card is then drawn at random from the remaining pack. Find the probability of getting :

(a) a face card

(b) an ace or a jack
rows.solution:
The face cards of spades are its king, queen and jack, so 3 cards are removed and \(52 - 3 = 49\) cards remain.

(a) The pack had 12 face cards; 3 are gone, leaving 9. \(P(\text{a face card}) = \dfrac{9}{49}\).

(b) All 4 aces remain, but the jack of spades was removed, so 3 jacks remain: \(4 + 3 = 7\) favourable cards. \(P(\text{an ace or a jack}) = \dfrac{7}{49} = \dfrac{1}{7}\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, PB is a tangent to the circle with centre O at B. AB is a chord of the circle of length 24 cm and at a distance of 5 cm from the centre of the circle. If the length PB of the tangent is 20 cm, find the length of OP.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the circle with centre O, chord AB with OM perpendicular to it at M, tangent PB at B and OP joined; the stem states every value needed (chord 24 cm, 5 cm from the centre, PB 20 cm). Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
Join OB. OM is the perpendicular from the centre to the chord AB, so it bisects the chord: \(AM = MB = \dfrac{24}{2} = 12\) cm, and \(OM = 5\) cm.

In right triangle OMB, \(OB = \sqrt{OM^2 + MB^2} = \sqrt{5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{169} = 13\) cm. This is the radius.

PB is a tangent at B, so the radius OB is perpendicular to it: \(\angle OBP = 90^\circ\).

In right triangle OBP, \(OP = \sqrt{OB^2 + PB^2} = \sqrt{13^2 + 20^2} = \sqrt{169 + 400} = \sqrt{569}\) cm \(\approx 23{\cdot}85\) cm.

rows.subtopic: Volume of a Combination of Solids
rows.stem: A solid toy is in the form of a hemisphere surmounted by a right circular cone. The height of the cone is 2 cm and the diameter of the base is 4 cm. Determine the volume of the toy. Also, find the surface area of the toy. (Take \(\pi = 3{\cdot}14\))
rows.solution:
The diameter of the base is 4 cm, so the radius of both the hemisphere and the cone's base is \(r = 2\) cm. The height of the cone is \(h = 2\) cm.

Volume of the toy \(= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h + \dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 3{\cdot}14 \times 2^2 \times 2 + \dfrac{2}{3} \times 3{\cdot}14 \times 2^3\)

\(= \dfrac{3{\cdot}14}{3}(8 + 16) = 3{\cdot}14 \times 8 = 25{\cdot}12\ \text{cm}^3\).

The slant height of the cone is \(l = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2} = 2\sqrt{2}\) cm.

The surface of the toy is the curved surface of the cone together with the curved surface of the hemisphere (the shared circular base is hidden inside):

Surface area \(= \pi r l + 2\pi r^2 = 3{\cdot}14 \times 2 \times 2\sqrt{2} + 2 \times 3{\cdot}14 \times 2^2 = 12{\cdot}56\sqrt{2} + 25{\cdot}12\)

\(= 12{\cdot}56\left(2 + \sqrt{2}\right)\ \text{cm}^2 \approx 42{\cdot}88\ \text{cm}^2\) (taking \(\sqrt{2} \approx 1{\cdot}414\)).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: The students of a class are made to stand equally in rows. If 3 students are extra in each row, there would be 1 row less. If 3 students are less in a row, there would be 2 more rows. Find the number of students in the class.
rows.solution:
Let there be x students in each row and y rows, so the class has \(xy\) students.

With 3 more students in each row there is 1 row less: \((x + 3)(y - 1) = xy\). Expanding, \(xy - x + 3y - 3 = xy\), so \(x - 3y + 3 = 0\) ... (i)

With 3 fewer students in each row there are 2 more rows: \((x - 3)(y + 2) = xy\). Expanding, \(xy + 2x - 3y - 6 = xy\), so \(2x - 3y - 6 = 0\) ... (ii)

Subtracting (i) from (ii): \(x - 9 = 0\), so \(x = 9\). Then from (i), \(9 - 3y + 3 = 0\) and \(y = 4\).

(Check: \(12 \times 3 = 36\) and \(6 \times 6 = 36\).)

So the class has \(9 \times 4 = 36\) students.
